claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature accelerates the coupled degradation of a multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The primary cause of the accelerated coupled degradation is galvanic corrosion between the alloy's different phases.
Potential differences between the phases produce the galvanic corrosion effect.
Multiphase HEA structures can have poorer corrosion resistance than single-phase HEA structures because of galvanic corrosion effects.
Elevated temperature promotes formation of an unstable passive film on a eutectic high-entropy alloy in a corrosive environment.
Galvanic coupling between phases causes the passive film to become unstable.
Mechanical wear ruptures the unstable passive film.
Rupture of the passive film increases the wear rate.
The multiphase eutectic alloy will have a higher wear rate than the single-phase or non-galvanically coupled baseline under otherwise identical conditions.
The multiphase eutectic alloy will have a higher corrosion rate than the single-phase or non-galvanically coupled baseline under otherwise identical conditions.
Total coupled degradation will be greater for the multiphase eutectic alloy than for the baseline.
A single-phase high-entropy alloy can serve as a baseline representing the absence of interphase galvanic corrosion.
Comparing multiphase and single-phase high-entropy alloys under the same exposure conditions can distinguish the proposed galvanic mechanism.
Failure of the multiphase alloy to show significantly higher wear and corrosion rates than the single-phase alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
